title: Quasi-coherent cohomology comparison along affine maps of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be affine, meaning representable with affine scheme base changes, and let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $H^q(X,M)=R^q\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},M)$ for cohomology of the underlying additive sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then, for every $q\ge0$, the canonical cohomology edge map $$H^q(X,f_*F)\longrightarrow H^q(Y,F)$$ is an isomorphism. Direct image is for the induced morphism of ringed small etale topoi.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-higher-direct-image-vanishing] to the given affine map $f:Y\to X$ and quasi-coherent module $F$. For the underlying additive sheaf $A=F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ it gives $R^bf_*A=0$ for every $b>0$. Its hypotheses are precisely affineness and quasi-coherence already assumed here; neither Noetherianity nor separation of the spaces is needed.

Use the abelian-sheaf Leray specialization of [det-thm-groth-ss] for the induced morphism of small etale topoi, forgetting the structure rings. It gives the first-quadrant sequence $E_2^{a,b}=H^a(X,R^bf_*A)\Rightarrow H^{a+b}(Y,A)$. The direct image of the underlying additive sheaf of $F$ is the underlying additive sheaf of $f_*F$: both assign to an etale test scheme $U\to X$ the additive group of $F(U\times_XY)$; the module direct image only equips this group with its scalar action. Thus the bottom row is exactly the cohomology of $f_*F$ meant in the statement. This uses global sections of the topoi; it does not assume that $X$ or $Y$ is a scheme or is a terminal object of its scheme-valued small etale site.

source.place: Tag 0732, lemma-Leray, and Tag 0733, lemma-apply-Leray (1), as invoked in Tag 0D2U.

proof.text: The positive rows of this spectral sequence are zero by step 1, since cohomology of the zero sheaf is zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse] to conclude that the bottom edge $H^q(X,f_*F)=E_2^{q,0}\to H^q(Y,F)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$. This is the canonical Leray edge, hence the edge map in the statement. In degree zero it is the defining identification $\Gamma(X,f_*F)=\Gamma(Y,F)$; in positive degrees the cited row-collapse result identifies that same edge with the inclusion of the sole nonzero associated-graded piece of the finite abutment filtration.
